answer: The network maps numbered stone ledges along one observation ridge and lets each earning key lease exactly one slot with a posted bond. A roaming falcon scout later drops a fresh nonce onto that ledge; only the leaseholder can return a signature bound to the slot number before it expires. Two keys that share a slot-bound reply, or a silent leaseholder, lose the bond and the ledge is re-auctioned. A sybil farm must therefore buy N scarce ledges and staff N operators for live nonce catches; extra cloned keys have no shelf left to rent.
